newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram "done well" for firms - FICCI.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram "done well" for firms - FICCI.

text.p: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) on Friday welcomed the government's 1997/98 (April-March) budget, saying it addressed the needs of the corporate sector.
FICCI vice president Sudhir Jalan said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had "done well" in cutting the domestic corporate tax to 35 percent from 40 percent.
"But we were expecting it will be reduced to 30 percent. Maybe he will do it in the next budget," Jalan said.

FICCI member K.N. Memani said: "I am very happy with the budget. Most of the expectations of the corporate sector have been met with the exception of the tax over distribution of dividend and carryover of MAT."
He was referring to the minimum alternate tax (MAT), which was introduced last year and retained in the 1997/98 budget.
FICCI member K.S. Mehta said: "MAT should have been done away with but what has been done is better than the punitive impact of the present form of MAT."
FICCI members said a breakthrough proposed by the Chidambaram was to widen the tax base and restructure the personal tax structure.
